faqs.q: What is the Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain and what is it used for?
faqs.a: The Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain is a five-link adaptor that steps a stud link chain down through enlarged and end links to a shackle or connector. It is used where stud link mooring chain meets a large-bore shackle or connector. It is part of the Indus offshore mooring chain range. See the [offshore mooring chain](/c/offshore-mooring-chain) shelf for the full range.

faqs.q: What sizes does the Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain come in?
faqs.a: The Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain is made to the chain it joins, so there is no fixed size range. The drawing gives every dimension as a multiple of the chain diameter D, so one design covers the whole range of chain sizes. Tell us the chain diameter and grade and we send the dimensioned drawing and weight with the quotation.

faqs.q: How do I specify the Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain?
faqs.a: State the chain diameter, grade (ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S or R5), whether it is stud link or studless, the length and the class or API certificate you need for the Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain. Match the grade and diameter to the chain on each side so the joint is as strong as the line. Send the mooring drawing if you have one and we check the make-up.

faqs.q: What is the load rating of the Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain?
faqs.a: No load rating is published for the Five-Link Adaptor in the listing, so the rating follows the chain grade and diameter and is confirmed with the quotation. It is made to the chain it joins, so it carries the same grade and test loads as that chain. Proof and breaking loads are test values, not working loads.

faqs.q: How do I order the Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain?
faqs.a: Send the chain diameter, grade, type and the class or API certificate you need, and we quote the Five-Link Adaptor with the drawing and certificate. Because it is made to the chain it joins there is no fixed part number, so the quotation carries the confirmed reference. Include the connector or shackle it must reach.

faqs.q: How does the Five-Link Adaptor differ from the Three-Link Adaptor?
faqs.a: The Five-Link Adaptor steps stud link chain down through enlarged and end links to a shackle or connector, while the Three-Link Adaptor is a short adaptor of common, enlarged and end links that joins studless chain to stud link chain. Choose on whether you are changing chain type or reaching a large-bore fitting. See the [Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain](/p/three-link-adaptor-studless-to-stud-link-mooring-chain) for its own details.

faqs.q: What grade and material is the Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain made in?
faqs.a: The Five-Link Adaptor is made in the grade and diameter of the chain it joins: ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S or R5. Say which grade the chain is, and whether it is stud link or studless, when you enquire. Material and heat treatment follow the grade.

faqs.q: What certificate comes with the Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain?
faqs.a: A classification-society certificate (ABS, BV, DNV, LR and others) is available on request for the Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain. State the class or API certificate you need when you enquire. The certificate follows the chain grade and the mooring design.

faqs.q: What does the Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain connect to?
faqs.a: The Five-Link Adaptor joins stud link mooring chain to a shackle or connector with a larger bore than the chain links. The enlarged links bridge the size step, so state the fitting as well as the chain size. Match the grade on both sides. Related: [mooring connectors](/c/mooring-connectors).

faqs.q: How should the Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain be inspected?
faqs.a: Inspect the Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain for wear, corrosion, deformation and link damage before it is made up and at each service interval, against the mooring design. Test loads are not working loads: design the mooring with the class or API safety factor applied. Replace a damaged link instead of repairing it.

faqs.q: What is Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5 and what is it used for?
faqs.a: Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain is stud link mooring chain for offshore units and floating production moorings, in API ORQ and IACS W22 grades R3 to R5. It is supplied with the rule proof and minimum breaking load for each diameter. The listing covers 60 sizes, one Indus part number each. See the [offshore mooring chain](/c/offshore-mooring-chain) shelf for chain tails and adaptors.

faqs.q: What sizes does Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5 come in?
faqs.a: Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain comes in 60 sizes, from 1-7/16″ (36 mm) to 205 mm. Every size has its own Indus part number, from IH-MR-MC-SL-0360 to IH-MR-MC-SL-2050. Weight per metre in the table runs 28 to 694. The links-per-shot column runs from 33 to 189.

faqs.q: How do I choose the diameter and grade of Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5?
faqs.a: Choose the diameter and grade of Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain from the design mooring load, then apply the class or API safety factor, because the listed loads are test loads, not working loads. State the diameter, grade (ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S or R5), stud link or studless, the length and the class or API certificate you need. For example the 105 mm size lists a minimum breaking load of 10,754 kN in R4 and 8,753 kN in R3. See our [guide to chain grades R3, R4 and R5](/blog/offshore-mooring-chain-grades-r3-r4-r5).

faqs.q: What are the proof and breaking loads of Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5?
faqs.a: Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain lists R4 minimum breaking loads from 1,460 to 31,781 kN and R4 proof loads from 1,151 to 25,054 kN across its sizes. R3 breaking load runs 1,188 to 25,866 kN and R5 1,705 to 37,116 kN. They are the classification-society test loads of IACS UR W22 (API Spec 2F for ORQ), not working loads: a mooring is designed with the class or API safety factor applied.

faqs.q: How do I read the Indus part number for Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5?
faqs.a: The last four digits of the Indus part number for Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain give the chain diameter in tenths of a millimetre. For example IH-MR-MC-SL-0360 is the 36 mm size, IH-MR-MC-SL-1050 the 105 mm size and IH-MR-MC-SL-2050 the 205 mm size. Quote the part number from the size table, or send the size and rating you need.

faqs.q: How does Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5 compare with studless chain?
faqs.a: Stud link chain differs from studless chain mainly in its proof load: from grade R3S up, IACS UR W22 sets a lower proof-load factor for studless chain than for stud link chain of the same grade. The minimum breaking load is the same for both. In R4 at 105 mm, Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain lists a proof load of 8,478 kN. Choose on the mooring design, the permanent or temporary service and the certificate required. See the [Studless Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5](/p/studless-offshore-mooring-chain-grades-orq-r3-r3s-r4-r4s-and-r5).

faqs.q: Which grades does Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5 come in?
faqs.a: Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain comes in grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5, listed in the size table for every size. At 36 mm the minimum breaking load rises through the grades: ORQ 1,124, R3 1,188, R3S 1,327, R4 1,460, R4S 1,620 and R5 1,705 kN. Say which grade you need on the enquiry; the diameter alone does not fix the strength.

faqs.q: What certificate and standard apply to Stud Link Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5?

The loads were checked size by size against the rule formula and against two chain makers' tables. State the class or API certificate you need when you enquire. Our [guide to chain marking and certificates](/blog/anchor-chain-marking-and-certificates) explains what each mark means.

faqs.q: Which grades does Studless Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5 come in?
faqs.a: Studless Offshore Mooring Chain comes in grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5, listed in the size table for every size. At 36 mm the minimum breaking load rises through the grades: ORQ 1,124, R3 1,188, R3S 1,327, R4 1,460, R4S 1,620 and R5 1,705 kN. Say which grade you need on the enquiry; the diameter alone does not fix the strength.

faqs.q: What certificate and standard apply to Studless Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5?
faqs.a: A classification-society certificate (ABS, BV, DNV, LR and others) is available on request for Studless Offshore Mooring Chain, and the proof and breaking loads follow IACS UR W22, with API Spec 2F for ORQ. The loads were checked size by size against the rule formula and against two chain makers' tables. State the class or API certificate you need when you enquire. Our [guide to chain marking and certificates](/blog/anchor-chain-marking-and-certificates) explains what each mark means.

faqs.q: What fittings connect to Studless Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5?
faqs.a: Studless Offshore Mooring Chain is joined to shackles, connectors and the rest of the mooring line through adaptors such as the five-link adaptor or three-link adaptor. The adaptor steps the chain through enlarged and end links to the fitting, so match the diameter and grade. Our connectors range covers the shackles and links that complete a mooring. See the [five-link adaptor](/p/five-link-adaptor-mooring-chain) and our [mooring connectors](/c/mooring-connectors).

faqs.q: How should Studless Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5 be inspected and tested?
faqs.a: Chain is proof tested and its breaking load verified to the class rule, and in service it should be inspected for wear, corrosion and link damage against the mooring design. Proof and breaking loads are test values, not working loads. The class or API certificate you specify sets which tests and marks the chain carries. Our [guide to proof, break and NDT testing](/blog/anchor-chain-testing-proof-break-ndt) covers the test regime.

faqs.q: Where is Studless Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5 used?
faqs.a: Studless Offshore Mooring Chain is used for permanent offshore moorings. Link size and grade follow the mooring design, with the safety factor applied to the listed test loads. Our [guide to stud link versus studless chain](/blog/stud-link-vs-studless-chain) explains the choice.

faqs.q: Does Indus stock Studless Offshore Mooring Chain — Grades ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S and R5 in Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes, the Studless Offshore Mooring Chain is held in stock at our Dubai, UAE warehouse and ships worldwide with the best lead times. [Request a quotation](/contact) with the part numbers and quantities you need.

faqs.q: What is the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain and what is it used for?
faqs.a: The Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain is a short adaptor of common, enlarged and end links that joins studless mooring chain to stud link chain and its fittings. It is used where a mooring line changes from studless to stud link chain. It is part of the Indus offshore mooring chain range. See the [offshore mooring chain](/c/offshore-mooring-chain) shelf for the full range.

faqs.q: What sizes does the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain come in?
faqs.a: The Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain is made to the chain it joins, so there is no fixed size range. The drawing gives every dimension as a multiple of the chain diameter D, so one design covers the whole range of chain sizes. Tell us the chain diameter and grade and we send the dimensioned drawing and weight with the quotation.

faqs.q: How do I specify the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain?
faqs.a: State the chain diameter, grade (ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S or R5), whether it is stud link or studless, the length and the class or API certificate you need for the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain. Match the grade and diameter to the chain on each side so the joint is as strong as the line. Send the mooring drawing if you have one and we check the make-up.

faqs.q: What is the load rating of the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain?
faqs.a: No load rating is published for the Three-Link Adaptor in the listing, so the rating follows the chain grade and diameter and is confirmed with the quotation. It is made to the chain it joins, so it carries the same grade and test loads as that chain. From grade R3S up, studless chain has a lower proof-load factor than stud link, so state which side governs.

faqs.q: How do I order the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain?
faqs.a: Send the chain diameter and grade, which side is studless and which stud link, and the class or API certificate you need, and we quote the Three-Link Adaptor with the drawing and certificate. Because it is made to the chain it joins there is no fixed part number. Include the length of line either side if it matters.

faqs.q: How does the Three-Link Adaptor differ from the Five-Link Adaptor?
faqs.a: The Three-Link Adaptor is a short adaptor of common, enlarged and end links that joins studless chain to stud link chain, while the Five-Link Adaptor steps stud link chain down through enlarged and end links to a shackle or connector. Choose the three-link adaptor when changing chain type and the five-link adaptor to reach a fitting. See the [Five-Link Adaptor — Mooring Chain](/p/five-link-adaptor-mooring-chain) for its own details.

faqs.q: What grade and material is the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain made in?
faqs.a: The Three-Link Adaptor is made in the grade and diameter of the chain it joins: ORQ, R3, R3S, R4, R4S or R5. Say which grade the chain is on each side when you enquire. Material and heat treatment follow the grade.

faqs.q: What certificate comes with the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain?
faqs.a: A classification-society certificate (ABS, BV, DNV, LR and others) is available on request for the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain. State the class or API certificate you need when you enquire. The certificate follows the chain grade and the mooring design.

faqs.q: What does the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain connect to?
faqs.a: The Three-Link Adaptor joins studless mooring chain to stud link chain, and through that chain to its fittings. Both sides must match in diameter and grade. See the guide on stud link versus studless chain for why the two differ. Related: [mooring connectors](/c/mooring-connectors).

faqs.q: How should the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain be inspected?
faqs.a: Inspect the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain for wear, corrosion, deformation and link damage before it is made up and at each service interval, against the mooring design. Test loads are not working loads: design the mooring with the class or API safety factor applied. Replace a damaged link instead of repairing it.

faqs.q: Where is the Three-Link Adaptor — Studless to Stud Link Mooring Chain used?
faqs.a: The Three-Link Adaptor is used where a mooring changes from studless chain to stud link chain. It is typical at transitions between the permanent studless section and stud link near the anchor or fairlead. Our [guide to stud link versus studless chain](/blog/stud-link-vs-studless-chain) gives the background.
